title: Stratum Surge Dashboard and Burst Heuristics
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design a compact, operator-focused dashboard (Stratum Surge) for Dedicated GPU capacity teams that surfaces pool health, autoscale intent, and burst scheduling heuristics. The goal is to reduce cognitive load during incidents and provide safe, reversible controls for short-term surge while showing estimated cost delta and SLO impact.
background_and_motivation: Operators currently flip between heatmap pages, raw metrics, and a separate autoscale policy editor. This leads to slow reaction during transient load spikes. We need a single surface that shows current pool readiness, recommended burst envelope, and a lightweight preview of cost/latency trade-offs before applying changes.
design_goals: Make health at-a-glance: a single line of primary indicators for each pool (utilization, tail-latency, error-rate, node-liveness)
Provide a safe burst workflow: suggest burst sizes/durations, show hysteresis, and require explicit confirm with rollback timer
Surface estimated cost delta and SLO risk for any autoscale or burst edit
Allow quick switch between ‘Diagnostic’ (expanded metrics) and ‘Action’ (compact controls) modes
Make the UI keyboard-and-screen-reader friendly for SREs in on-call rotations
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrates both Diagnostic and Action modes for at least three pool sizes (small/medium/large)
Prototype includes a burst preview modal showing cost delta, expected queue reduction, and rollback ETA
Design tokens and spacing match console-2025 design system; components annotated for dev handoff
Design review signed off by PM (Maya Rodriguez) and Eng owner (Rohit Menon)
Accessibility checklist completed (contrast, keyboard focus, ARIA hints)
key_decisions_and_tradeoffs: We prioritized a single-line primary health row over a large heatmap to speed incident triage. Tradeoff: less visual density for long-term trend analysis (kept Diagnostic mode for that).
Burst is limited to predefined envelopes (small/medium/large) instead of arbitrary node counts to simplify backend validation and rollback logic.
Cost preview uses an estimated per-minute billing model (not exact) to avoid blocking on backend billing integration for initial launch.
implementation_notes: Frontend should reuse cardi-list row components and the compact metric sparklines. Autoscale API contract: PATCH /pools/:id/scale with {mode: 'burst', envelope: 'medium', duration_minutes: 30, rollback_minutes: 15}. Team will add server-side validation to prevent overlapping bursts.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Operators could overuse burst and increase cost. Mitigation: default to conservative envelopes, require two-step confirm, and show estimated cost in the confirm modal.
Risk: Incomplete telemetry may show stale health. Mitigation: show telemetry freshness badges and 'Last updated' timestamps prominently.
Risk: Complexity for on-call SREs. Mitigation: create a one-click ‘revert last burst’ action with clear timeline and audit trail.
